title: Alertness, Distractions & Phones
whatItIs: Safe driving needs concentration at all times. Phones, loud music, eating, smoking and arguing can all distract you.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT use a hand-held phone or similar device while driving, even when stopped at lights or in a queue.

keyFacts: You may call 999 or 112 on a hand-held phone in a real emergency, if it is unsafe or impractical to stop.

keyFacts.text: You MUST exercise proper control of your vehicle at all times, even when using a hands-free phone.

keyFacts: It's far safer not to use any phone while driving: find a safe place to stop first, or use voicemail.
Loud music, eating, smoking and arguing passengers can all distract you.

visual.caption: A hand-held phone at the wheel costs

items.label: Fixed penalty
items.note: Up to £1,000 if it goes to court

items.label: New drivers
items.note: 6 points within 2 years of passing and you lose your licence

a.label: Hand-held phone
points: Even stopped at lights or in a queue

b.label: Hands-free phone
points: You must stay in proper control

onTheTest.question: When may you use a hand-held mobile phone while driving?
options: To call 999 in an emergency when it is unsafe to stop
When you are stopped at traffic lights
When you are queuing in slow traffic
To check your sat nav for a moment
onTheTest.why: You can call 999 or 112 in a genuine emergency if it's unsafe or impractical to stop. Being stopped in traffic still counts as driving.

traps: Stopped at the lights still counts as driving.
Hands-free is legal, but it is not risk-free.
New drivers: one phone offence (6 points) is enough to lose your licence.
